title: U.S. House · Ohio's 3rd District
area: Central Ohio, including most of Columbus

context.text: The Cook Political Report rates the 3rd District D+21, a safely Democratic-leaning seat.

summary.text: Beatty is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Ohio's 3rd District, first elected in 2012 and in office since 2013. Before Congress she served five terms in the Ohio House of Representatives, where she became the first woman to lead the House Democrats, and worked as a senior vice president at Ohio State University. She is seeking re-election.

background.text: Born in Montgomery County, Ohio, and graduated from Nettie Lee Roth High School.

Earned a bachelor's degree from Central State University and a master's degree from Wright State University; according to her congressional website, she also completed all requirements except the dissertation for a doctorate at the University of Cincinnati.
Worked as a college professor and in human services before entering elected office.
Served in the Ohio House of Representatives from 1999 to 2008 (five terms, per her congressional website), rising to become the first female Democratic House Leader in Ohio's history.
Served as senior vice president of outreach and engagement at The Ohio State University before her election to Congress.

Has represented Ohio's 3rd District in the U.S. House since 2013. Her congressional website lists her as a member of the Committee on Financial Services, with membership on its Housing and Insurance and Oversight and Investigations subcommittees.

According to her congressional website, her bipartisan child sex trafficking legislation passed the House in 2015 and was signed into law as part of the Justice for Victims of Trafficking Act, and her REPAY Supplies Act of 2015 (a permanent teacher-expense tax deduction) was included in the PATH Act of 2015.

Her congressional website lists involvement in The Links, Inc., Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Inc., the National Coalition of 100 Black Women, the Columbus Urban League and the American Heart Association, where she previously served on the board; it states she is married to attorney Otto Beatty, Jr.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Financial Services in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

Served on the Committee on Financial Services in the 118th Congress (2023-2024), including as ranking member of the Subcommittee on National Security, Illicit Finance, and International Financial Institutions.

summary.text: Dulaney is the Republican nominee and a business owner who grew up in Birmingham, Alabama. He also ran in the 2020 Republican primary for this seat. His campaign website lists housing affordability, policing, homelessness and addiction, and property taxes as issues.

background.text: Grew up in Birmingham, Alabama; his professional experience includes owning his own business.
Ran in the April 28, 2020 Republican primary for Ohio's 3rd District and lost to Mark Richardson, receiving 13.6% of the vote (1,797 votes).
In his 2020 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, described himself as a single father raising three daughters and as holding traditional values.
Won the uncontested May 5, 2026 Republican primary with 15,779 votes.

priorities.text: Campaign website lists gentrification and the affordable-housing crisis in the district as issues, citing regional projections of population growth.
Campaign website calls for a 'better relationship with our police force' and addressing homelessness and opioid-addiction rehabilitation.
Campaign website lists property taxes and home-improvement grants as an issue.
